Show the current function body again

menu.reconcile_note: sym.sess_ispoweruser is a two-line wrapper. It calls sym.sess_validate and returns the unsigned test uVar1 < 100. Blind, this is need-more-context, because the verdict depends entirely on what sess_validate returns for an unauthenticated or expired session. Delivering the body of sym.sess_validate (0x40bd78) resolves it: sess_validate reads the external sentry session store (through find_sentry and rw_sentry) and returns the stored session level on success, or 0xffffffff (-1) when the session is missing, invalid or expired. Because the wrapper compares as unsigned, 0xffffffff is not < 100, so the unauthenticated session is denied. Only a valid session with a low numeric level (0..99, meaning high privilege) is granted power-user. So the original enforces a real session-backed privilege check and resolves to not-vulnerable. This one artifact is both necessary and sufficient, so min_rounds = 1. The same body does not neutralize the mutant. The mutant keeps this exact wrapper but injects `if ((int32_t)uVar1 < 0) return true;` before the original return, which grants power-user on precisely the -1 sentinel path that sess_validate uses for the unauthenticated or expired session. Learning that sess_validate returns -1 for that case only makes the escalation clearer, so the mutant still resolves to vulnerable. The off-target items are real same-binary functions away from the verdict path: sym.sess_validate_privatekey (0x40ba18, the separate private-key check the caller also requires), sym.find_sentry (0x40b0b8, the deeper session-store reader called inside sess_validate), and the caller sym.pigwidgeoncgi_main (0x40f120). None of them is needed to decide this wrapper, so picking one ends the unit.
